info.title: Schautrack API
info.summary: Read and write your Schautrack calorie, weight, todo, and food data.
info.description:
The Schautrack public API.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `/openapi.json` and `/docs` requires a
**personal access token**, sent as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer stk_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Create one under **Settings → API tokens**. The token is shown once and cannot be
retrieved again. Tokens can be scoped and given an expiry, and can be revoked at
any time.

Session cookies are **not** accepted here. Because the API never treats a cookie
as authentication, no cross-site request can carry credentials to it — which is
why there is no CSRF token to manage.

## Scopes

A token carries an explicit set of scopes. A `:write` scope implies the
matching `:read`, so `entries:write` alone is enough to both read and
write entries.

Calling an endpoint without its scope returns `403` with a
`required_scope` field naming what is missing.

## Errors

Errors are [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) problem details,
served as `application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "https://schautrack.com/problems/validation-failed",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "One or more macro values are out of range.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/entries",
  "invalid_params": [{ "name": "protein_g", "reason": "must be between 0 and 999" }]
}
```

Branch on `type`, not on `detail`: the type URI is stable, the prose is not.

The `type` URIs are **stable identifiers, not endpoints**. Every instance,
self-hosted ones included, emits the same `https://schautrack.com/problems/…`
URIs on purpose, so a client can recognise a problem type without knowing which
host produced it. Do not dereference them, and do not expect a self-hosted
instance to rewrite them to its own domain. This document's `servers` URL,
by contrast, *is* an endpoint, and always names the instance that served it.

## Dates and time zones

Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` in the **account's** time zone. Omitting a date means
"today" for that account, not for the machine making the request. Timestamps are
RFC 3339 UTC; each entry also carries `local_time` rendered in the account's
zone.

## Pagination

`GET /entries` and `GET /weight` are paginated by keyset. Pass the
`next_cursor` from a response back as `cursor` to fetch the next
page; stop when `has_more` is false. Cursors are opaque — do not
construct them.

## Retrying safely

Every `PUT` here is idempotent by construction: the URL names the resource
and the body states the desired state, so repeating one changes nothing.

`POST` is different. If a request to create an entry times out, you cannot
know whether it landed. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header — any string you
generate once per logical operation and reuse when retrying:

```
Idempotency-Key: 5f8c1e2a-meal-breakfast-2026-08-05
```

The first request executes and its response is stored. Any retry with the same
key replays that response, with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, instead of
logging the meal twice. Reusing a key with a *different* body returns `409`
rather than silently discarding the new request. Keys are remembered for 24
hours. A request that fails releases its key, so the retry is a fresh attempt
rather than a replay of the error.

Every endpoint that creates something accepts the header: `POST /entries`,
`POST /todos`, `POST /saved-foods`, and
`POST /saved-foods/{id}/track`. The operation parameter lists say which,
and they are not advisory — the one `POST` that does not honour the header
(`POST /ai/estimate`) rejects it with `400` instead of ignoring it.
An accepted request is therefore always a request whose retry semantics are
what you asked for.

## Rate limits

Three limits apply: one per IP address, one per token, and — on the two
endpoints that cost real resources — one per account. `POST /ai/estimate`
and `GET /barcode/{code}` reach a paid provider and a third-party food
database respectively, so they are capped at the same rate the app's own UI
gets rather than at the API-wide ceiling; a token is not a cheaper route to
them than a browser.

Exceeding any of the three returns `429` with a `Retry-After`
header giving the number of seconds until the window reopens. Honour it rather
than retrying blindly.

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `entries:read` | Read calorie entries and their macros. |
| `entries:write` | Create, update, and delete calorie entries. |
| `weight:read` | Read weight entries. |
| `weight:write` | Record and delete weight entries. |
| `todos:read` | Read todos and their completion state. |
| `todos:write` | Create, update, delete, and complete todos. |
| `foods:read` | Read saved foods. |
| `foods:write` | Create, update, and delete saved foods. |
| `notes:read` | Read daily notes. |
| `notes:write` | Write daily notes. |
| `plan:read` | Read the weight-loss plan, its goal, and its projections. |
| `links:read` | Read data that linked accounts have shared with you. |
| `settings:read` | Read account settings (goal, timezone, units, language). |
| `settings:write` | Change account settings (goal, timezone, units, language). |
| `ai:estimate` | Estimate nutrition from a food photo. Costs money per call — grant sparingly. |

post.summary: Estimate nutrition from a food photo
post.description: Requires the `ai:estimate` scope, which no other scope implies — every call spends the operator's AI budget, so it must be granted deliberately. The account's daily AI limit applies here exactly as it does in the app, as does a per-account rate limit matching the app's own estimate endpoint — this is not a cheaper path to the provider. Returns 404 when no AI provider is configured; `GET /me` reports whether it is, under `server.features.ai_estimate`. Honours `Idempotency-Key`, and this is the endpoint it matters most on: a retried estimate would spend the AI budget twice and burn a second slot in the account's daily cap, for a photo already analysed.

get.description: Returns this OpenAPI description. Needs no token.

Read-only. Unlike the app's own plan endpoint, this one never writes — a `plan:read` token cannot change state, so a goal that has been reached is reported but not transitioned.

**Your own plan only, deliberately.** This endpoint does not accept `user`: the plan is a projection over body metrics and a weight goal, and account linking has no share category covering either. A linked account's weight readings are readable via `GET /weight?user=`; the plan built from them is not.

Most-used first, then most-recently-used, then newest first. Not paginated: an account holds at most 200 saved foods, so this always returns the complete set.

**Your own foods only, deliberately.** This endpoint does not accept `user`: account linking shares nutrition, weight, todos, and notes, and saved foods are none of those, so there is no share category that could authorize reading another account's. Passing `user` is ignored.

get.description: Pass the same `user` you listed with — a date from `GET /weight?user=42` is a reading on account 42, and without `?user=42` this looks in your own readings and returns 404. `unit` is always the unit of whoever the reading belongs to; readings are never converted.

parameters.description: Read a linked account's data instead of your own. Pass the `user_id` from `GET /links`. Requires the `links:read` scope AND that the account shares this category with you; otherwise 403. Shared data is read-only — no write endpoint accepts this.

BarcodeProduct.description: The product as resolved from OpenFoodFacts, or a not-found result.

BodyComposition.description: Body composition derived from the most recent body-fat reading. That reading can be older than the current weight — body composition is measured less often — so `date` says when it was taken.

ageDays.description: Whole days between `date` and today. Negative is possible and means fresh: `date` is the account's local date while today is the server's, so a few hours of timezone skew can put the reading marginally ahead.

bodyFatPct.description: Body fat as a percentage of total mass. A percentage, so never unit-converted.

category.description: The band `bodyFatPct` falls in for this sex: `essential`, `athletic`, `fitness`, `average` or `obese`. `null` when the sex is unknown — the bands genuinely differ by sex, so no label is given rather than a wrong one.

date.description: The day the body-fat reading was recorded.

fatMass.description: Fat mass at that reading. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

leanMass.description: Fat-free mass at that reading. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

stale.description: Whether the reading is too old to choose the BMR formula (older than 90 days). A stale reading is still reported — it is the account's most recent measurement — but `computed.bmrFormula` falls back to `mifflin_st_jeor` instead of `katch_mcardle`.

Completion.description: A todo's completion state on a date.

completed.description: `true` marks it done on this date, `false` clears it.

CurvePoint.description: One week of the projected curve.

week.description: Weeks from now. Week 0 is the starting weight.

weight.description: Projected weight that week. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

calories.description: Energy in kilocalories. May be negative to record a correction.

date.description: The day this entry belongs to, in the account's time zone.

local_time.description: `created_at` rendered as HH:MM in the account's time zone.

name.description: What was eaten. Up to 120 bytes.

EntryInput.description: A new calorie entry. Supply `calories`, at least one macro, or both.

date.description: Defaults to today in the account's time zone.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Opaque — do not parse.

EntryPatch.description: Fields to change. Omit a field to leave it alone; send `null` to clear a macro or the name.

calories.description: Energy in kilocalories. Rejected while the account computes calories from macros.

date.description: Move the entry to another day.

Estimate.description: The model's nutrition estimate. Shape follows the app's AI response.

image.description: The photo as a `data:image/...;base64,...` URI. Maximum 10 MB.

HealthyRange.description: The weight range corresponding to a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 at the account's height.

max.description: Upper bound. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

min.description: Lower bound. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

Link.description: A linked account, from your point of view.

label.description: The name you gave this link, if any.

shares_to_them.description: What you share back with them.

shares_with_me.description: What this account shares WITH you — the only categories `?user=` will serve.

timezone.description: Their IANA time zone. Their timestamps are rendered in it, not yours.

user_id.description: Pass this as the `user` query parameter on a read endpoint.

Macros.description: Macronutrients in grams. `null` means the macro was not recorded, which is distinct from a recorded zero.

Me.description: The authenticated account, the token, and the account's enabled features.

features.description: Per-account opt-ins that change how the rest of the API behaves. Read-only: they are switched in the app's settings, not through this API. Every field is always present.

auto_calc_calories.description: Calories are computed from macros. When `true`, `POST /entries` derives `calories` from the macros it was given rather than trusting the value sent, and `PATCH /entries/{id}` rejects `calories` with a `422`.

body_fat.description: Body-fat readings are enabled. When `false` a stored reading is not shown in the app.

macros.description: At least one macro (protein, carbs, fat, fiber, sugar) is enabled for this account, so macro values are shown in the app.

notes.description: Daily notes are enabled. When `false`, `GET` and `PUT /notes/{date}` answer `409`.

todos.description: Todos are enabled in the app. The todo endpoints work either way, but a todo created while this is `false` is invisible to the user.

features.description: Which OPTIONAL endpoints this deployment actually serves. Separate from the account-level `features` below on purpose: this is how the operator configured the instance, that is what the user switched on, and a client needs to tell "you turned this off" apart from "this server does not offer it". Both fields are always present.

ai_estimate.description: An AI provider is configured, so `POST /ai/estimate` is live. The account's daily cap still applies on top.

barcode.description: `GET /barcode/{code}` will attempt a lookup. When `false` it answers 404 `feature-disabled`.

today.description: Today's date in the account's time zone.

token.description: The token that authenticated this request.

expires_at.description: When it stops working. `null` means never.

name.description: The label given when it was created.

user.description: The account this token belongs to.

timezone.description: IANA time zone. Determines what `today` and every bare date mean.

weight_unit.description: The unit weight readings are stored in.

content.description: The note. Empty when no note is set.

updated_at.description: When it was last written (UTC). `null` when there is no note.

NoteInput.description: The note's full content. Writing an empty string deletes it.

Plan.description: The weight-loss plan: body metrics, active goal, computed budget, projected curve, and trend analysis. Every field is always present; those that depend on data the account has not supplied are `null`. Every weight-valued field is in the unit named by `unit` — read it rather than assuming kilograms.

bmi.description: Body mass index. `null` without both a height and a weight.

composition.description: Derived from the most recent body-fat reading. `null` when none was recorded.

computed.description: The budget and projection. `null` unless the body metrics are complete AND an active goal has a usable pace.

currentCalorieGoal.description: The account's daily calorie target as it stands now, which need not equal `computed.budgetKcal` — the recommendation is only applied when the user accepts it.

currentWeight.description: The most recent weight reading. `null` when none is logged. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

disclaimer.description: Fixed text to show alongside the numbers. The plan is an estimate, not medical advice.

goal.description: The active weight goal. `null` when none is set.

healthyRange.description: The healthy weight range for the account's height. `null` without a height and a weight.

metrics.description: The body metrics the plan is computed from.

series.description: Logged weight readings from the last 180 days, oldest first.

trend.description: Observed progress. `null` when no goal is set; present but flagged `insufficient_data` when there are too few readings.

unit.description: The unit every weight-valued field in this payload is in: `kg` or `lb`. The plan is computed in kilograms and converted once, on the way out, to the account's configured unit; this field records which one that was, so the numbers can be read without a second call to `/me`.

warnings.description: Safety notes about this plan. Empty when there is nothing to flag.

PlanComputed.description: The energy budget and the projection it produces.

bmrFormula.description: Which estimator produced `bmr`: `katch_mcardle` when a body-fat reading was available (it works off lean mass, the more accurate basis), `mifflin_st_jeor` otherwise.

budgetClamped.description: Whether the budget was raised to the safe floor for this sex. The matching `budget_clamped` warning is also emitted.

etaDate.description: The date `etaWeeks` lands on. `null` when the ETA is not a finite number.

etaWeeks.description: Weeks to the target at that pace.

planCurve.description: Projected weight week by week. It decelerates: BMR is recomputed at each simulated weight, so the deficit shrinks as the weight does. Stops at the target, at a plateau, or after 160 weeks.

ratePerWeek.description: The goal's pace per week. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

tdee.description: Total daily energy expenditure: BMR times the activity factor, kcal/day.

PlanMetrics.description: The body metrics the plan is computed from. Each is `null` until the account supplies it; they are set in the app, not over this API.

activityLevel.description: `sedentary`, `light`, `moderate`, `active` or `very_active`. Decides the multiplier applied to BMR to reach TDEE.

birthYear.description: Year of birth; age is derived from it.

complete.description: Whether all four are set. `computed` stays `null` while this is `false`.

heightCm.description: Height in centimetres. Never converted — this is not a weight.

sex.description: `male`, `female` or `other`. Used by the Mifflin–St Jeor formula and the calorie floor.

PlanTrend.description: Observed progress: a least-squares fit over the readings from the last 30 days. Independent of the body metrics, so it works even when `computed` is `null`.

hasData.description: Whether there were enough readings — two, at least a week apart — to fit a line.

projectedDate.description: The date `projectedWeeks` lands on. `null` when it cannot be projected.

projectedWeeks.description: Weeks to the target at the observed rate. `-1` when it cannot be projected.

slopePerWeek.description: Fitted change per week, negative when losing. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

status.description: Progress against the plan's pace: `ahead` from 110%, `on_track` from 85%, `behind` below that. `stalled` when the fitted change is under 0.05 per week, `wrong_direction` when it moves away from the target, `insufficient_data` when `hasData` is false.

PlanWarning.description: A safety note about the plan. Branch on `code`; `message` is English prose that can change.

code.description: What is being flagged: `budget_clamped` (the budget was raised to the safe floor), `aggressive_rate` (the pace exceeds 1% of body weight per week), `target_underweight` or `target_obese` (the target weight falls in that BMI band).

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

instance.description: The request path that produced it.

required_scope.description: Present on 403s: the scope the token is missing.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the problem type. Branch on this.

emoji.description: Optional emoji shown next to the name.

name.description: Food name. Unique per account, case-insensitively.

use_count.description: How many units have been tracked from this food.

name.description: Food name, up to 80 bytes. Must be unique for the account.

SavedFoodList.description: Saved foods, most-used first. Never partial.

data.description: Every saved food on the account.

SavedFoodPatch.description: Fields to change. `null` clears a nullable field.

type.description: `daily` every day; `weekly` on the listed days.

SeriesPoint.description: One logged weight reading, as charted.

bodyFat.description: Body fat percentage recorded with it. Absent when the scale reported weight only.

weight.description: The reading. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

SettingsPatch.description: Account settings to change. Omit a field to leave it alone.

language.description: UI language: one of en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pl, pt. `null` restores automatic.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. Decides what every bare date means.

weight_unit.description: Display unit. Changing it does NOT convert stored readings — they are kept as entered.

time_of_day.description: Optional HH:MM the todo is due at.

TodoDay.description: A todo as it applies to one date.

completed.description: Whether it is done on this date.

missed_since.description: The first scheduled day missed, if the streak is broken.

streak.description: Consecutive scheduled days completed, ending on this date.

time_of_day.description: HH:MM it is due at, if set.

data.description: Timed todos first, in time order, then untimed.

name.description: What to do. Up to 100 bytes.

date.description: Defaults to today in the account's time zone.

Weight.description: A weight reading. One per account per day.

body_fat.description: Body fat as a percentage, or `null` when the day carries no measurement.

date.description: The day this reading belongs to.

unit.description: The account's weight unit. Readings are stored as entered and never converted.

WeightGoal.description: The active weight goal, echoed in the account's unit. Read-only here: setting a goal has real health implications, so it stays in the app where the numbers can be explained.

achieved_at.description: When the goal was met (UTC). Absent while it is active.

activity_level.description: The activity level recorded with the goal: `sedentary`, `light`, `moderate`, `active` or `very_active`.

pace_mode.description: `rate` sets a weekly pace directly; `date` derives one from `target_date`.

rate_per_week.description: The requested pace per week. Present when `pace_mode` is `rate`. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field. Renamed from `rate_kg_per_week`, which was not necessarily kilograms: the goal is stored and echoed in the account's own unit. `PUT /plan/goal` still accepts the old key on input so existing clients keep working.

start_date.description: The day the goal was set.

start_weight.description: Weight when the goal was set. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

status.description: `active`, `achieved` or `abandoned` — always `active` here, since this endpoint only returns the active goal.

target_date.description: The requested finish date. Present when `pace_mode` is `date`.

target_weight.description: The target. In the unit given by the plan's `unit` field.

body_fat.description: Body fat as a percentage, rounded to one decimal. **Omit** to leave any stored reading for that day untouched — which is what makes a weight-only scale integration safe to retry. Send `null` to clear it. Writing a value switches the account's body-fat field on if it was off, so the reading is visible in the app; clearing never switches it back off.

weight.description: The reading, in the account's unit.

WeightList.description: A page of weight readings, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Opaque — do not parse.

bearerAuth.description: A personal access token from Settings → API tokens. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer stk_…`.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed — unparseable JSON, an unknown field, or a bad query parameter.

Conflict.description: The request collides with existing state — a duplicate name, a limit already reached, or a feature not enabled.

InsufficientScope.description: The token is valid but lacks the scope this endpoint requires. The `required_scope` field names it.

NotFound.description: No such resource, or it belongs to another account.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body exceeds the 1 MB limit. Attached to every operation that takes a body — the cap is enforced in the decoder, not per endpoint.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. The `Retry-After` header gives the number of seconds until the window reopens.

Unauthorized.description: No token, or the token is unknown, revoked, or expired.

Unprocessable.description: The request is well-formed but its values are rejected. `invalid_params` lists the offending fields.
